newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean insurers at risk if government aid ends.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean insurers at risk if government aid ends.

text.p: Life insurers could be troubled if South Korea halts the "protection-for-regulation" policy that has played a vital role in the nation's rapid economic growth for the past three decades, an industry leader said on Monday.

"The policy of offering protection in return for controls has so far worked. But now the environment is changing and the government will have to give up the policy in the near future," a director of the Korea Life Insurance Association told Reuters.
Under the "protection-for-regulation" policy, if a company faces major trouble, the government intervenes and bails it out.
Analysts criticise the policy which they say has deprived companies of the opportunity to learn from insolvencies.
"As a result of continued deregulation and liberalisation, companies now have to look at market conditions, rather than the government, for their survival," the director said.
The director, who declined to be identified, said South Korean insurance reserves had already been hit as a result of heavy capital investment.
Data compiled by the Association showed 17 of South Korea's 33 life insurers had a policy reserve shortage totalling 714.5 billion won (US$801 billion) as of the end of March.
Hankuk Life Insurance Co topped the list with 97.2 billion won, followed by Dong Ah Life Insurance Co with 94.7 billion and Handuk Life Insurance Co with 75.7 billion.
Early last year, the 17 companies were ordered to increase their paid-up capital to clear the shortfall, at that time valued at a total of 1.2 trillion won.
By March, none of the 17 firms had done so and faced penalties, ranging from warnings to limits in their business activities, an association official said.
Concerns over the solvency of South Korean life insurers have been raised in the wake of the 200 billion yen (US$1.58 billion) failure in April of Japan's Nissan Mutual Life.
"If you really want to see an industry that is hanging by a thread, take a look at South Korea," one analyst who declined to be identified said.
South Korea is Asia's second biggest life insurance market behind Japan with a premium volume of US$45.7 billion in 1995, the last year for which figures are available.
Sigma, the research arm of Swiss Reinsurance, ranks South Korea as the world's sixth largest life insurance market.
